- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to match sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend (e.g., after sentiment shift); for first 3–5 forecast days, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast, avoiding over-smoothing.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates mean-reversion targets; add 0.5–2% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, to account for lagged rebound.
